_meta.STATUS: SUPERSEDED — DO NOT TREAT AS CURRENT
_meta.engine_note: Which engine produced these numbers. verify_benchmark.py checks the optional agent block ONLY when the results file carries a matching _provenance.engine stamp. Mtime cannot do this job: the agent file is always written by a separate earlier invocation, so any timestamp cutoff either rejects a legitimate fresh file or accepts a stale one. The 2026-08-06 defect was a leftover sulci-minilm run checked against these builtin-tfidf numbers, reporting six of eight rows as [OK].
_meta.description: HISTORICAL TF-IDF benchmark numbers, measured on the PRE-2026-08-04 corpus. That corpus warmed every group, so every test query had a same-group twin already cached, a hit was always available, and the hit rate could only be high. It is kept for provenance: the retired 85.9% / 0.74ms / 3,000x / $21 site claims came from here, and so did the 31.11% false-positive rate that was never published beside them.
_meta.why_it_is_still_here: scripts/verify_benchmark.py and `make benchmark-verify` compare against this file, and .github/workflows/benchmark.yml runs the benchmark. This file was NOT unreferenced -- it was RED. Deleting it would silently remove a check; leaving it undated let it read as current. It is dated instead.
_meta.known_drift_2026_08_06: Verified on a clean tree: stateless hit_rate 0.8588 -> 0.6551, false_positive_rate 0.3111 -> 0.4418, cost_reduction_pct 85.88 -> 65.51. This drift predates the 2026-08-06 context work; it is the #127/#128 corpus rebuild, which added held-out groups and NEAR_MISS pairs so that 39% of test queries have no correct answer cached. The numbers below describe a corpus that no longer exists.
_meta.to_regenerate: python benchmark/run.py --no-sweep --context, then copy the measured values from benchmark/results/summary.json and context_summary.json. Do this only once, deliberately, and record the date and commit here -- a baseline that is refreshed whenever it goes red is not a baseline.
_meta.tolerance_notes: Counts may drift by ±2 across platforms (Linux vs macOS) due to dict-iteration tie-breaks. Headline percentages match exactly. Latency varies by machine; not part of regression check.
_meta.agent_workload_note: agent_workload is checked ONLY when benchmark/run.py was invoked with --agent. RETRACTED 2026-08-04: this note previously asserted that real-MiniLM mode gives "~60-75% aggregate vs ~95% TF-IDF". That was never measured. Measured 2026-08-04 it gives 95.0% -- the same as TF-IDF, which is therefore not an upper bound on this workload. That single sentence is where the 60-75% figure in the site hero, the SI pitch deck and the email signature came from. Do not restore it.

context_aware._note: Measured with NO held-out sessions, so false_hit_rate did not exist and is unmeasurable from this run. 125 follow-ups across 5 domains. accuracy_delta_pct 20.8 and the customer_support improvement of 0.56 below are the retired +20.8pp and +56pp site claims, at their source.
